data.question: How did chemists establish whether the loss of mass in combustion reflected the escape of a substance from the burning body or the absorption of something from the air, and what settled the dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Lavoisier's calcination trials were carried out in open crucibles standing in the free atmosphere.
  • Henry Cavendish discovered oxygen in 1766 by heating red calx of mercury.
data.a_html:
The question of what is lost and what is gained in burning was, for the better part of a century, a dispute about the direction of a transfer. Georg Ernst Stahl formulated the phlogiston theory in the early eighteenth century, and on his account combustion was a giving off: a burning body released a material substance called phlogiston into the air. Whereas that doctrine made the burning body the donor, Jean Rey had argued in 1630 that calcined tin gained weight by taking up matter from the air, and it was only after Stahl's system had become the common property of chemists that this contrary suggestion was seriously revived. Rey's conjecture, in any case, preceded by nearly a century and a half the experiment that would decide between the two accounts.

Lavoisier heated tin in a hermetically sealed glass retort. There was no change in the total mass of the sealed retort after the metal had been calcined inside it. Lavoisier stated the principle that the total mass of matter is conserved in a chemical change, offering it as a general axiom of his chemistry. The balance had more to tell. When Lavoisier broke the seal of the retort after heating, air rushed into the vessel, and that inrush shows that the weight gained by the metal equalled the weight of air lost from the sealed vessel.

A difficulty attends the usual description of this work. Lavoisier's calcination trials were carried out in open crucibles standing in the free atmosphere; but a crucible standing open to the surrounding air cannot be squared with the heating of the tin in a hermetically sealed glass retort, since one and the same trial cannot have been both closed against the air and exposed to it.

Joseph Priestley obtained a new gas in 1774 by heating mercuric oxide with a burning lens, and as a result he called that gas dephlogisticated air. Henry Cavendish discovered oxygen in 1766 by heating red calx of mercury, and this rules out the first procurement of the gas from the mercury calx having come eight years later at Priestley's hands: the discovery cannot belong to Cavendish in 1766 and also be the work of 1774.

The outcome admits of just two descriptions, of which exactly one must hold and not both. Either phlogiston theory was ultimately retained as the accepted account of combustion, or — even though the gas drawn from mercuric oxide was christened dephlogisticated air, in the very idiom of the older doctrine — phlogiston theory was ultimately abandoned in favour of the oxygen theory of combustion. The weighings in closed vessels, rather than any single polemic, are what made the choice between them unavoidable.

data.question: How do scholars decide whether a shared cultural practice found in two widely separated societies spread by contact or arose independently, and what kind of finding settles such a dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue.
  • Sweet potato was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia.
data.a_html:
The choice between diffusion and independent invention is decided by the pattern of evidence rather than by the intrinsic plausibility of the trait itself. Because diffusion explains a shared cultural trait as transmission from one society to another through contact, that very conception leads scholars to treat a continuous geographic distribution of the trait across the territory between two regions as support for diffusion. Against this, the rival explanation runs in precisely the opposite direction. Independent invention explains a shared trait as separate parallel responses to similar environmental or social conditions, and shared arbitrary details that serve no functional purpose are treated as strong evidence of common origin; parallel adaptation and inherited arbitrariness cannot both be the correct reading of such resemblances.

That same evidential principle — the weight placed on arbitrary, functionless correspondences — shows why loanwords shared between the languages of two societies indicate direct contact between their speakers. Two further instruments do different kinds of work. Ancient DNA analysis can detect genomic admixture produced by contact between two populations; radiocarbon dating, by contrast, establishes the relative chronology of a trait's first appearance in each region. data.question: How do forensic engineers establish whether a bridge collapse originated in a design deficiency or in subsequent construction and maintenance practice when the design firm and the contractor each attribute the failure to the other?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Concrete cylinder tests showed compressive strengths forty percent below specification.
  • The probable cause was overloading of the deck by parked construction equipment.
data.a_html:
Attributing a bridge failure to design or to execution is a problem of reconciling the physical record of the structure with the paper record of the decisions made about it, and the Florida International University walkway offers a model of how the two are brought together. When the pedestrian bridge collapsed onto an open roadway during construction, the gravity of the event led the National Transportation Safety Board to take charge of the federal investigation. The investigators' first obligation was to establish precisely what the structure was doing in the period leading up to the failure. Structural cracking was documented at the north end of the span in the days before the collapse, and workers were re-tensioning post-tensioning rods in a diagonal member at the moment the span fell; cracking already recorded at the north end rules out re-tensioning work being underway in that diagonal as the structure came down.

Out of that record two candidate explanations arise, and at least one of them is true, perhaps both: the contractor left the span unshored during the re-tensioning operation; the design drawings understated the shear demand at the critical truss node. The federal inquiry so constituted led directly to the principal technical exercise of the case. Forensic engineers rebuilt the structural model using finite element analysis to recompute member capacities, and tensile testing of recovered reinforcing steel showed that it met the specified yield strength; a model rebuilt to recompute capacities cannot be squared with recovered bar that conformed to its specified yield. Those recomputed capacities confirm the understatement of shear demand in the drawings. By contrast with the reinforcing steel, the concrete as placed was deficient: concrete cylinder tests showed compressive strengths forty percent below specification.

The documentary and regulatory record runs parallel to this laboratory work. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration issued citations to the construction contractor after the collapse. The peer reviewer's scope of work omitted a capacity check of the critical nodal region. The citations issued against the contractor show that the span was indeed left without shoring while the rods were being re-tensioned.

Only against an assembled record of this kind can a probable cause be stated, and the competing versions must then be measured against one another. The probable cause was overloading of the deck by parked construction equipment. The probable cause of the collapse was errors in the design firm's load and capacity calculations; overloading by parked equipment and miscalculation of loads and capacities cannot both have brought the span down. That is to say, the failure is attributable to the engineer of record miscalculating structural demand and resistance. The gap left in the peer reviewer's scope indicates exactly that attribution, since the one independent check capable of catching the error at the node was never carried out. Where the design firm and the contractor each point at the other, it is this interlocking of recomputed mechanics, material testing and the audit trail of review that decides between them.

data.question: How do scholars decide whether a shared cultural practice found in two widely separated societies spread by contact or arose independently, and what kind of finding settles such a dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue.
  • Sweet potato was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia.
data.a_html:
The choice between diffusion and independent invention is decided by the pattern of evidence rather than by the intrinsic plausibility of the trait itself. Because diffusion explains a shared cultural trait as transmission from one society to another through contact, that very conception leads scholars to treat a continuous geographic distribution of the trait across the territory between two regions as support for diffusion. Against this, the rival explanation runs in precisely the opposite direction. Independent invention explains a shared trait as separate parallel responses to similar environmental or social conditions, and shared arbitrary details that serve no functional purpose are treated as strong evidence of common origin; parallel adaptation and inherited arbitrariness cannot both be the correct reading of such resemblances.

That same evidential principle — the weight placed on arbitrary, functionless correspondences — shows why loanwords shared between the languages of two societies indicate direct contact between their speakers. Two further instruments do different kinds of work. Ancient DNA analysis can detect genomic admixture produced by contact between two populations; radiocarbon dating, by contrast, establishes the relative chronology of a trait's first appearance in each region. That chronological role cannot be squared with the fact that radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue; the two accounts of the method cannot both be true.

The Polynesian sweet potato shows how a dispute of this kind is brought to a close. Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is native to tropical America. The crop was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia, a homeland that rules out an American nativity, since the plant cannot have originated in both places. Charred sweet potato remains from Mangaia in the Cook Islands were radiocarbon dated to about AD 1000, and herbarium specimens collected during early European voyages have been used to reconstruct sweet potato lineages in Polynesia; the Mangaian date and the herbarium reconstruction cannot both stand.

Some nine centuries after those tubers were charred and buried, the question of transport across the Pacific was addressed by experiment rather than by excavation. Thor Heyerdahl's 1947 Kon-Tiki raft voyage travelled from Peru to the Tuamotu Islands. A demonstration that a voyage is feasible does not establish that the transfer actually occurred. A controversy of this type is therefore closed only by a find that ties the two societies to each other directly — a dated specimen, a genome, a borrowed word — and not by a demonstration of what was merely within reach.

data.question: How did biologists establish whether the genetic material of the cell is DNA or protein, and what reasoning settled the dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Griffith performed his pneumococcal transformation experiment in 1944.
  • Hershey and Chase used carbon-14 to tag the protein component of the bacteriophage.
data.a_html:
The question of whether heredity resided in nucleic acid or in protein was settled by a chain of experiments on bacteria and on the viruses that infect them. Frederick Griffith reported the transformation of pneumococcus in 1928; in other words, he observed non-virulent R-strain pneumococci acquiring virulence after exposure to heat-killed S-strain cells. Griffith performed his pneumococcal transformation experiment in 1944, a dating that cannot be squared with a report of the same observation appearing in 1928. Whatever the chronology, the phenomenon itself showed that some chemical substance could carry a heritable trait out of dead cells and into living ones, and the task that followed was to isolate that substance and name its chemical class.

Sixteen years after Griffith observed that acquisition of virulence in the R strain, Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty published their identification of the transforming principle in 1944. Phoebus Levene's tetranucleotide hypothesis depicted DNA as a monotonous repeating molecule. That hypothesis caused protein to be the favoured candidate for the hereditary material among biologists before 1944.

The Avery group treated their transforming extract with proteolytic enzymes such as trypsin and chymotrypsin. By contrast, treatment of the transforming extract with deoxyribonuclease destroyed its transforming activity altogether. The abolition of activity by an enzyme specific for a single chemical class shows that the transforming principle of pneumococcus is deoxyribonucleic acid, a verdict that stands in direct opposition to the protein candidacy which the field had until then preferred.

Corroboration came from a wholly different system. Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase published their bacteriophage blender experiment in 1952. Hershey and Chase labelled bacteriophage DNA with the radioisotope phosphorus-32, and as a result most of the phosphorus-32 label was recovered in the pellet of infected bacteria. Hershey and Chase labelled the bacteriophage protein coat with the radioisotope sulfur-35. They used carbon-14 to tag the protein component of the bacteriophage; these two accounts of how the coat was marked cannot both be true. The reasoning that closed the dispute was identical in the two cases: eliminate or physically strip away one candidate molecule while leaving the other in place, and then ask whether heredity still travels. Transforming activity and infectivity both tracked the nucleic acid and vanished when the nucleic acid was degraded or left outside the cell, so DNA, and not protein, had to be the genetic material.

data.question: How does a court decide whether a defendant's conduct or an intervening third party's act bears legal responsibility for a plaintiff's injury when the evidentiary record supports two incompatible accounts of the sequence of events?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The defendant bears the burden of disproving causation once the plaintiff establishes an injury.
  • A criminal act committed by a third party always severs the chain of causation.
data.a_html:
A court faced with two incompatible accounts of how an injury came about begins by dividing its task. Factual causation and legal causation are analysed as two separate inquiries, and that division shows what the first of them demands: the but-for test asks whether the injury would have occurred in the absence of the defendant's conduct. The plaintiff carries the burden of proving causation in a civil negligence action. The defendant bears the burden of disproving causation once the plaintiff establishes an injury.

The standard of proof for causation in a civil action is the balance of probabilities; that is, the reviewing court concluded that the plaintiff was required to prove causation only on the balance of probabilities, and the placing of the burden of causation on the plaintiff is precisely what shows that conclusion to be correct. The record establishes at least one of two things, and perhaps both: the stair tread was broken at the time of the plaintiff's fall, or the warning barricade had been removed from the stairway before the plaintiff's fall. Either state of affairs puts the occupier's conduct squarely within the sequence that ends in the plaintiff's injury.

That the plaintiff need prove causation to no higher a level than the balance of probabilities carries a direct consequence for where responsibility for choosing between the two versions of events lies. The trial judge resolves conflicts between irreconcilable witness accounts, and that primacy in the assessment of testimony has led appellate courts to defer to trial findings of fact absent palpable and overriding error. The practical effect is that the party who loses the factual contest at first instance faces a correspondingly narrow path on review, and the chosen narrative of the sequence of events becomes the foundation on which the legal analysis proceeds.

The second inquiry is different in kind, for it asks not whether the defendant's conduct figured in the sequence but whether responsibility should attach to it once a third party has acted. A superseding cause relieves the original defendant of liability for the resulting injury. A criminal act committed by a third party always severs the chain of causation. An intervening act that is reasonably foreseeable, by contrast with one that supersedes, leaves the defendant's liability intact. That principle indicates the outcome reached on appeal: the appellate court ultimately held that the third party's act was reasonably foreseeable and did not break the chain of causation, a holding that cannot be squared with any rule under which a third party's criminal act invariably severs the chain of causation. The defendant who creates a hazard and leaves it exposed therefore answers for the injury that follows, whatever hand last touched the scene.

data.question: How do archaeologists adjudicate between rival interpretations of a site's abandonment when stratigraphic evidence, environmental proxies, and textual sources appear to point in different directions?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Radiocarbon dating returns calendar dates accurate to a single year.
  • The principle of documentary primacy requires excavators to treat textual sources as overriding stratigraphic evidence.
data.a_html:
Adjudication begins with an audit of resolution: the first question is which line of evidence can be dated most tightly, and over what interval. Stratigraphic sequences establish the relative order in which deposits at a site accumulated. Because that order fixes which deposit is earlier and which is later, it resulted in a marked tightening of the absolute chronology attached to each individual deposit. Radiocarbon dating provides absolute age estimates for organic material recovered from stratified deposits, and the accumulation of such estimates led to Bayesian statistical modelling, which combines radiocarbon measurements with stratigraphic ordering to narrow date ranges. In the proxy record, the chronological resolution is commonly coarser than that of excavated stratigraphy. Radiocarbon dating returns calendar dates accurate to a single year; single-year accuracy of that kind and the narrowing of broad probability ranges by combining measurements with stratigraphic order cannot both obtain.

Resolution also governs how proxy records may be recruited into an explanation. Whereas the chronological resolution of proxy sequences is coarse, dendrochronology yields annually resolved dates for preserved wood samples. That annual precision is what shows that tree-ring records from the northern Southwest document a severe drought in the late thirteenth century AD. A regional dry spell is not in itself an abandonment, so the inference must run through the settlement's own economy: the drought caused environmental stress that reduced the agricultural output which sustained the settlement, and at least one of that failing subsistence base and a disruption of the settlement's exchange networks by political conflict in the region was at work in the final decades, perhaps both.

The deposits themselves then constrain which of these narratives the proxies may be made to support. Either the final occupation layer of the settlement contains burned destruction debris, or it contains no traces of burning: one of the two descriptions is correct and they cannot both be, so the terminal section discriminates directly between a violent end and an orderly departure. Where a question of this form is settled by the excavated profile rather than by a climate curve, the stratigraphic record operates as a check on reconstructions built from environmental data alone.

Textual sources are weighed last, and their weight is not fixed in advance of excavation. The principle of documentary primacy requires excavators to treat textual sources as overriding stratigraphic evidence; such overriding authority cannot be squared with the release of excavated sections and context records for other specialists to reinterpret, since material put into circulation for reinterpretation is not material already subordinated to a chronicle's testimony. Excavation reports publish primary stratigraphic data so that other researchers can reassess the interpretations, and that practice has led to competing interpretations of abandonment being tested through peer review in academic journals. Adjudication, in the end, consists in ranking the resolution of each line of evidence and submitting that ranking to open scrutiny.

data.question: How did scholars resolve the long-running dispute over whether the Vinland Map is an authentic medieval document or a modern forgery?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The map was donated to the British Library in 1965.
  • Walter McCrone identified lead white as the anachronistic pigment present in the map's ink.
data.a_html:
The Vinland Map is a world map that depicts a landmass labelled "Vinlanda Insula" to the west of Greenland, and from the moment of its appearance its status divided cartographic historians. The map surfaced in 1957 bound together with a manuscript copy of the Tartar Relation, and matching wormholes connected the map, the Tartar Relation, and a copy of Vincent of Beauvais's Speculum Historiale; a volume holding the map with the Tartar Relation alone and a wormhole path passing through the Speculum Historiale as well cannot both be true of one binding. Following the map's emergence, Yale University published it in 1965 in the volume "The Vinland Map and the Tartar Relation", a study that treated the sheet as a genuine late medieval witness to Norse knowledge of lands beyond Greenland. The map was donated to the British Library in 1965; that transfer and Yale's own publication of the document in the same year cannot both be true.

Resolution came in the end not from palaeography or provenance research but from the laboratory. Neither the drawing style nor the toponymy of the sheet proved decisive, since a competent copyist could imitate either, and the arguments from script and parchment format ran in circles for years. Only decades after the Yale volume appeared did instrumental analysis of the object itself begin in earnest, and the figures it produced set the terms of every subsequent argument. Radiocarbon dating carried out in 2002 placed the map's parchment at about the year 1434. Anatase pigment of the kind found in the ink was first manufactured commercially in the 1920s.

The ink, rather than the parchment, became the focus of controversy. Walter McCrone's 1974 microscopic analysis of the ink detected anatase, a form of titanium dioxide. Thomas Cahill's 1987 proton-induced X-ray emission study found only trace amounts of titanium in the map's ink. Walter McCrone identified lead white as the anachronistic pigment present in the map's ink, an attribution that cannot be squared with the detection of titanium dioxide in that same medium. Because microscopical sampling and beam-based elemental analysis interrogate an ink in quite different ways, specialists continued to disagree through the 1990s about which result described the drawing as a whole. Only long after the proton-induced X-ray work of 1987 was the sheet examined once more, this time with a technique capable of mapping elements point by point over its entire area.

Conservators at Yale's Beinecke Library scanned the map with X-ray fluorescence imaging in 2021, and that scan brought to light titanium compounds in ink lines across the whole surface of the map. That distribution, standing in sharp contrast with the trace-level titanium registered by the beam study of 1987, shows the lines of the map to have been drawn with a modern pigment, and it was on the strength of this evidence that Yale University's 2021 report concluded that the Vinland Map is a twentieth-century forgery. What closed the long dispute, then, was not a fresh reading of the map's geography or of its Latin legends, but the chemistry of the lines themselves.

data.question: How do forensic engineers establish whether a bridge collapse originated in a design deficiency or in inadequate maintenance by the owner, and what evidence allows a tribunal to settle the matter?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Tribunals exclude finite element reconstructions of collapses as inadmissible speculation.
  • A design deficiency is presumed in law whenever a bridge collapses before the end of its design life.
data.a_html:
The inquiry into whether a bridge collapse originated in a design deficiency or in the owner's maintenance regime begins at the debris field, with the steel itself. Forensic engineers recover, tag, and catalogue the fracture surfaces of every failed member from the collapsed span; because that inventory exists, a fractographic examination can be carried out that distinguishes progressive fatigue cracking from single-event overload fracture. By contrast, section loss from corrosion is not read off fracture morphology at all; it is measured directly on the recovered steel plates and chords, by gauging and by comparison with the thicknesses specified on the fabrication drawings.

The analytical half of the exercise proceeds in a fixed sequence. data.question: How does a court decide whether a defendant's conduct or an intervening third party's act is legally responsible for the plaintiff's injury when each side's expert offers an incompatible account of the sequence of events?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The burden of proving causation shifts to the defendant once a breach of duty is established.
  • A criminal act by a third party automatically relieves the defendant of all liability for the plaintiff's injury.
data.a_html:
A court confronted with duelling reconstructions of an accident does not begin by preferring one expert to the other; it begins by identifying the legal test that the evidence must satisfy and the party who must satisfy it. A plaintiff who must prove causation on the balance of probabilities cannot at the same time be afforded the material contribution test, which applies precisely where but-for causation cannot be established scientifically; the plaintiff does bear that balance-of-probabilities burden, and that test does apply in cases of scientific impossibility, but the one cannot be squared with the other. The but-for test, by contrast with the material contribution standard, asks whether the injury would have occurred in the absence of the defendant's conduct, a question that invites a counterfactual rather than a probabilistic judgment. Once a breach of duty is established, the burden of proving causation shifts to the defendant; that reallocation rules out any continuing requirement that the plaintiff establish causation to the balance of probabilities, and the two allocations cannot both govern a single trial.

The question of an intervening act proceeds along a second axis, concerned not with the sufficiency of proof but with the limits of attribution. Novus actus interveniens describes an intervening act that severs the causal connection between a breach and the harm. A reasonably foreseeable intervening act does not break the chain of causation. A criminal act by a third party automatically relieves the defendant of all liability for the plaintiff's injury, and that cannot be squared with the principle that an intervening act falling within the range of reasonable foresight leaves the causal chain unbroken. On the evidence accepted in this case, the third party's act broke the chain of causation; that is to say, the intervening act of the third party severed the legal link between the defendant's breach and the plaintiff's injury.

Both inquiries depend upon opinion evidence that has survived judicial scrutiny. Federal Rule of Evidence 702 governs the admissibility of expert opinion testimony, and it is from that provision that the authority to keep out an opinion resting on unreliable method flows. Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals established the trial judge's gatekeeping role over expert evidence, and as a result a trial judge may exclude expert testimony that rests on an unreliable methodology. The resolution of conflicting expert testimony is a question for the trier of fact.

Because the choice between competing expert reconstructions of the sequence of events falls to the fact-finder, the trial court ultimately held that the defendant's conduct remained a proximate cause of the plaintiff's injury. That holding and the severance of the legal link between the breach and the plaintiff's injury by the third party's act cannot both be true; a finding of continuing proximate cause rules out any such severance. The choice between incompatible narratives is thus made within the ordinary machinery of proof rather than by any special rule reserved for conflicts of expertise.

Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The burden of proving causation shifts to the defendant once a breach of duty is established.
  • A criminal act by a third party automatically relieves the defendant of all liability for the plaintiff's injury.
data.a_html:
A court confronted with duelling reconstructions of an accident does not begin by preferring one expert to the other; it begins by identifying the legal test that the evidence must satisfy and the party who must satisfy it. A plaintiff who must prove causation on the balance of probabilities cannot at the same time be afforded the material contribution test, which applies precisely where but-for causation cannot be established scientifically; the plaintiff does bear that balance-of-probabilities burden, and that test does apply in cases of scientific impossibility, but the one cannot be squared with the other. The but-for test, by contrast with the material contribution standard, asks whether the injury would have occurred in the absence of the defendant's conduct, a question that invites a counterfactual rather than a probabilistic judgment. Once a breach of duty is established, the burden of proving causation shifts to the defendant; that reallocation rules out any continuing requirement that the plaintiff establish causation to the balance of probabilities, and the two allocations cannot both govern a single trial.

The question of an intervening act proceeds along a second axis, concerned not with the sufficiency of proof but with the limits of attribution. Novus actus interveniens describes an intervening act that severs the causal connection between a breach and the harm. A reasonably foreseeable intervening act does not break the chain of causation. A criminal act by a third party automatically relieves the defendant of all liability for the plaintiff's injury, and that cannot be squared with the principle that an intervening act falling within the range of reasonable foresight leaves the causal chain unbroken. On the evidence accepted in this case, the third party's act broke the chain of causation; that is to say, the intervening act of the third party severed the legal link between the defendant's breach and the plaintiff's injury.

Both inquiries depend upon opinion evidence that has survived judicial scrutiny. Federal Rule of Evidence 702 governs the admissibility of expert opinion testimony, and it is from that provision that the authority to keep out an opinion resting on unreliable method flows. The power of a trial judge to exclude expert testimony that rests on an unreliable methodology was brought about by Daubert v. Merrell Dow Pharmaceuticals, which established the gatekeeping role of the trial judge over expert evidence. The resolution of conflicting expert testimony is a question for the trier of fact.

Because the choice between competing expert reconstructions of the sequence of events falls to the fact-finder, the trial court ultimately held that the defendant's conduct remained a proximate cause of the plaintiff's injury. That holding and the severance of the legal link between the breach and the plaintiff's injury by the third party's act cannot both be true; a finding of continuing proximate cause rules out any such severance. The choice between incompatible narratives is thus made within the ordinary machinery of proof rather than by any special rule reserved for conflicts of expertise.

data.question: How do sociologists adjudicate whether poor neighborhoods themselves shape residents' later life outcomes or whether the families who end up in such neighborhoods already differ in ways that produce those outcomes?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Sibling fixed-effects designs remove all unobserved confounding, including factors that change over time within a family.
  • Moving to Opportunity recruited families in all fifty states through a national lottery.
data.a_html:
Sociologists approach the neighborhood question as a problem of causal identification rather than of portraiture, and the field's answer has been assembled out of successive designs, each imposing a stricter standard on how a family came to live where it lives. The earliest generation of this work was devoted to measuring the social properties of places and relating them to outcomes recorded in those same places. Robert Sampson's Project on Human Development in Chicago Neighborhoods measured collective efficacy across Chicago neighborhoods, and those measurements show that higher collective efficacy was associated with lower rates of neighborhood violence.

Patrick Sharkey has documented multigenerational exposure to high-poverty neighborhoods among Black American families. That pattern of inherited place indicates that observational neighborhood studies are vulnerable to omitted variable bias from unmeasured parental traits, since the same families reappear in the same disadvantaged settings generation after generation. Precisely because unmeasured parental traits distort such estimates, Wodtke, Harding, and Elwert applied marginal structural models with inverse probability weighting to address time-varying confounding of neighborhood exposure. By contrast, sibling fixed-effects designs compare siblings whose childhoods were spent in neighborhoods of differing quality. Because every comparison is drawn within a single family, that design removes all unobserved confounding, including factors that change over time within a family.

Housing policy supplied leverage of a different kind, since the allocation of a scarce benefit by lottery converts the question of selection into a question of who was offered a chance to move. The Gautreaux program relocated Chicago public housing residents under a court-ordered desegregation remedy, and the Moving to Opportunity demonstration was mounted afterward. That demonstration randomly assigned housing voucher offers to low-income families in five U.S. cities, and as a result researchers were able to use the randomized voucher offer as an instrument for subsequent exposure to neighborhood poverty. Chetty, Hendren, and Katz found that children who moved to lower-poverty neighborhoods before age 13 earned more as adults.

The administrative details of that demonstration govern what can be inferred from it. Moving to Opportunity recruited families in all fifty states through a national lottery, a recruitment arrangement that cannot be squared with the confinement of randomized voucher offers to five metropolitan areas. Its enrollment structure admits exactly one of two possibilities: either the demonstration included a randomly assigned control group that received no new housing voucher, or every family enrolled in Moving to Opportunity received an experimental housing voucher; one of the two held, and they cannot both have held. Adjudication therefore turns on a single criterion, namely whether a given design makes neighborhood exposure independent of the family characteristics that would otherwise produce the outcome under study.

data.question: How do grid operators and regulators establish whether a large-scale blackout following a surge in wind and solar generation stemmed from the intermittency of those resources themselves or from deficiencies in transmission planning and protective settings, when the generators and the network operator advance opposing accounts?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The blackout occurred on 14 February 2017.
  • The Federal Court imposed penalties exceeding 200 million dollars on the wind farm operators.
data.a_html:
Where the generators and the network operator advance opposing accounts, the question is resolved not by aggregate statistics on the variability of wind and solar output but by reconstructing the disturbance second by second from fault recorders, protection event logs, high-speed SCADA telemetry and the performance standards each plant is registered to meet. Each party's narrative is then required to fit that reconstruction. A severe storm damaged transmission towers in South Australia on 28 September 2016, and the turbine protection settings permitted only a limited number of voltage dips before output was cut; storm forces that physically destroyed towers cannot be squared with protection settings that cut output only after a counted series of dips, so the two cannot both describe what initiated the event.

Resolving which mechanism was operative therefore begins with the condition of the network and the condition of the plant. At least one of two findings must hold, and conceivably both: the transmission towers were destroyed by tornado-strength winds, or the wind farms' low-voltage ride-through settings were configured below the required capability. The high-speed records then settle what the plant actually did. Voltage ride-through protection settings in the turbines triggered a sustained reduction in wind farm output, and as a result approximately 456 MW of wind generation was lost over about seven seconds. That rapid withdrawal of generation in turn left the Heywood Interconnector carrying more power than its design limit; that is, power flow on the Heywood Interconnector exceeded its rated capacity. Because the flow stood above the rating, the Heywood Interconnector to Victoria tripped after being overloaded.

South Australia was electrically separated from the rest of the National Electricity Market, and the under-frequency load shedding scheme did not arrest the frequency collapse after the separation; a genuine electrical separation from the interconnected market cannot be squared with a load shedding scheme that failed to halt the frequency collapse that followed, so one of the two must be wrong. The separation was itself brought about by the overloading and consequent trip of the interconnector, which is why investigators treat the interconnector's transfer limit, rather than resource variability as such, as the hinge of the cascade.

The market operator stated that the wind farms did not meet their registered generator performance standards. The blackout occurred on 14 February 2017. That finding of non-compliance with the registered standards resulted in the Federal Court imposing penalties exceeding 200 million dollars on the wind farm operators.

The methodological lesson is that intermittency and planning or protection deficiencies are distinguished by documentary evidence of what each element was configured to do and what it measurably did at each instant, not by the competing characterisations the parties bring to the inquiry.

data.question: How do sociologists adjudicate between the claim that neighborhood disadvantage itself shapes children's later life outcomes and the claim that such outcomes merely reflect the kinds of families who end up in those neighborhoods?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The Moving to Opportunity earnings gains were concentrated among children who moved after age 18.
  • The Project on Human Development in Chicago Neighborhoods randomly assigned families to neighborhoods with differing levels of collective efficacy.
data.a_html:
The dispute between neighborhood-effects researchers and their critics turns on a problem of inference rather than of measurement. Selection bias arises when families' unmeasured attributes determine which neighborhoods they enter; in other words, unmeasured parental characteristics influence which neighborhoods families move into. Faced with the familiar correlation between childhood address and adult attainment, sociologists must therefore establish that at least one of two things holds: either such unmeasured parental characteristics shape where families move, or neighborhood conditions exert a causal influence on children's adult earnings, and perhaps both hold at once. No cross-sectional association, however finely adjusted, can settle which of the two is doing the work.

Experimental design is the standard route out of this impasse, which is why the mechanics of particular programs matter so much. Either Moving to Opportunity allocated its housing vouchers to participating families by lottery, or placement in the Moving to Opportunity experimental group was determined by caseworker discretion rather than by lottery; one of these two descriptions must hold, and they cannot both hold. Allocation by lot, where it is genuinely achieved, results in randomized voucher assignment severing the link between family background and neighborhood context. That is to say, lottery-based allocation of housing vouchers makes a family's neighborhood statistically independent of its parental characteristics.

For this reason the long-run follow-up to that experiment supplies the evidence that confirms the causal claim about neighborhood conditions and children's adult earnings. Chetty, Hendren, and Katz reported that children who moved to low-poverty neighborhoods before age 13 earned more as adults, a pattern which shows that the Moving to Opportunity earnings gains were concentrated among children who moved after age 18. By contrast, the interim Moving to Opportunity evaluation found no significant effects of voucher receipt on adult employment or earnings, a reminder that timing and the age at which exposure occurs are integral to any causal verdict rather than incidental to it.

Observational designs enter the adjudication where experiments are unavailable or exhausted. The Project on Human Development in Chicago Neighborhoods measured collective efficacy across Chicago neighborhoods. Families in that study were randomly assigned to neighborhoods with differing levels of collective efficacy. Whereas that Chicago effort characterized communities in terms of collective efficacy, analyses of exposure duration have reached conclusions of a quite different kind, concerning educational attainment rather than the social organization of place. Wodtke, Harding, and Elwert applied marginal structural models to estimate the effects of sustained neighborhood exposure, and those estimates show that sustained exposure to disadvantaged neighborhoods reduced the probability of high school graduation. Adjudication between the causal and the selection account thus rests, in the end, on whether a given design can render neighborhood context independent of the families who sort into it.

data.question: How do engineers adjudicate between a latent software defect and a hardware fault when a distributed database silently corrupts records, and what evidence ultimately settles the attribution?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Byte-identical corruption across replicas in separate datacenters proves independent hardware failure.
  • ECC memory corrects all multi-bit errors within a single memory module.
data.a_html:
Adjudicating between a latent software defect and a hardware fault in a silently corrupting distributed database is a matter of pattern discrimination, and it begins with detection rather than with diagnosis. Background scrub jobs recompute stored checksums to detect silent corruption; only after such a job flags a mismatch do engineers compare the byte content of the same record across each of its replicas. The outcome of that comparison supplies the evidence that discriminates between the competing hypotheses. Byte-identical corruption on independent replicas points to a fault in the shared software path. Replica topology enters the picture as well: byte-identical corruption across replicas in separate datacenters proves independent hardware failure. By contrast, corruption isolated to a single replica on a single node points to a localized hardware fault. The question is never settled by the fact of corruption alone, but by its distribution across machines that share code yet share no silicon.

A second line of inquiry runs through the hardware telemetry gathered for the interval in which the scrub reported mismatches. ECC memory controllers log correctable single-bit error counts for each memory module. Vendors document the correction scheme in detail; ECC memory corrects all multi-bit errors within a single memory module. Those per-module records show that single-bit flips at arbitrary offsets are characteristic of DRAM faults. Engineers therefore read the counters alongside device firmware logs, looking for a module or a drive whose error rate rose in step with the first observed mismatch.

The signature recovered in the incident under review had a different shape entirely: the damaged bytes did not wander across the page but sat at predictable offsets. Corruption aligned to record and page boundaries is characteristic of a serialization defect, and that alignment showed that the storage engine's compaction code contained a latent defect which mishandled a rare offset case. Reproducing that offset case against a synthetic workload then took the argument out of the realm of inference, since the same mangled output appeared on hardware whose counters were clean.

At least one of two conditions therefore obtained: a latent defect in the compaction path, or an uncorrectable fault in the memory of node seven, and conceivably both at once. The memory module in node seven did have an uncorrectable hardware fault. Even though that module had failed outright, the post-incident review board concluded that the root cause was a latent software defect in the compaction path, because the boundary-aligned damage extended to replicas that shared no memory with node seven.

On the question of consequences, exactly one of two outcomes holds and the two cannot both be true: either every corrupted record was recoverable from backups and replica repair, or at least one corrupted record was permanently unrecoverable. What ultimately settles the attribution is the conjunction of three findings: the cross-replica byte comparison, the per-module error history, and a deterministic reproduction of the fault on hardware known to be sound.

data.question: How do oceanographers establish whether an abrupt regional shift in sea surface temperature reflects natural variability in ocean circulation or anthropogenic forcing, and how is a particular episode such as the North Atlantic "cold blob" adjudicated between those accounts?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Sea surface temperature in the cold blob region rose faster than the global mean over the twentieth century.
  • The RAPID array was installed in 1984 along the 45°N transect.
data.a_html:
Adjudicating an abrupt regional temperature anomaly between internal variability and forced change begins with fixing the observational pattern itself. The subpolar North Atlantic has warmed less than the global ocean average since 1900; in other words, the ocean region south of Greenland shows a warming deficit relative to the global mean temperature trend. Sea surface temperature in the cold blob region rose faster than the global mean over the twentieth century, and an excess of regional warming cannot be squared with a deficit over the same waters south of Greenland: the two descriptions cannot both hold.

The attribution problem is then posed over a system in which at least one of two contributions operates, and perhaps both: internal variability of ocean circulation contributes to the cold anomaly in the subpolar North Atlantic, and anthropogenic forcing contributes to that anomaly as well. The formal machinery for separating them is pattern-based. Optimal fingerprinting compares observed spatial patterns of temperature change with model-simulated responses to external forcing. CMIP6 models forced with rising greenhouse gas concentrations simulate a warming hole in the North Atlantic, which is strong evidence that anthropogenic forcing does contribute to the subpolar cold anomaly.

Measurements of the ice sheet and of regional surface salinity enter the assessment at this point. The IMBIE assessment estimated that Greenland lost roughly 3,900 gigatonnes of ice between 1992 and 2018. Surface salinity is tracked by hydrographic survey and Argo floats; meltwater from the Greenland Ice Sheet freshens the surface waters of the subpolar North Atlantic. Wintertime overturning in the Labrador Sea is gauged by repeat hydrography: reduced deep convection there weakens northward ocean heat transport.

Quantifying the circulation itself demands sustained instrumentation. The RAPID-MOCHA mooring array monitors the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation at 26.5°N. The RAPID array was installed in 1984 along the 45°N transect, a siting that cannot be reconciled with a monitoring line at 26.5°N; one or the other locates the moorings, not both. Whereas moored instruments gauge the modern overturning directly, the centuries preceding them are reconstructed from the seafloor. Sortable silt grain-size records serve as paleoceanographic proxies for past deep current strength, and such grain-size evidence indicates an AMOC weakening of about 15 percent since the mid-twentieth century, as Caesar and colleagues estimated. A decline of that magnitude is evidence that northward ocean heat transport has slackened as deep convection in the Labrador Sea has diminished. Adjudication of the cold blob thus rests on the joint verdict of fingerprint analysis, measured circulation and sedimentary reconstruction.

data.question: How did physicists adjudicate between the competing accounts of the 2011 OPERA result that neutrinos had outpaced light, and what finally settled whether the anomaly reflected new physics or an instrumental artifact?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The CERN-to-Gran Sasso baseline used in the OPERA measurement was 450 kilometres long.
  • The OPERA anomaly was traced to an error in the geodetic survey of the baseline distance.
data.a_html:
The 2011 anomaly was adjudicated in the way such disputes usually are: by interrogating every link in the measurement chain and by asking what else would have to be true if the result stood. The neutrinos studied by OPERA were produced in the CNGS beam at CERN. The flight path between the CERN source and the OPERA detector spanned about 730 kilometres. The CERN-to-Gran Sasso baseline used in the OPERA measurement was 450 kilometres long, and that length cannot be squared with a separation of some 730 kilometres, since no single flight path can have both extents.

OPERA reported in September 2011 that neutrinos arrived roughly 60 nanoseconds earlier than light would have, and the collaboration released that measurement as an arXiv preprint and invited independent scrutiny instead of claiming a discovery; a timing excess asserted that definitely and a refusal to claim the discovery it would constitute cannot both stand. The early-arrival figure, together with the choice to circulate it for outside checking rather than to proclaim a discovery, is what prompted the first theoretical reckoning: because a 60-nanosecond head start had been put into open circulation in precisely that provisional form, particle theorists set about deriving what such a beam would have to do on its way through the rock.

The OPERA timing chain depended on GPS satellite synchronisation between CERN and Gran Sasso. The baseline distance was fixed by geodetic surveying to an accuracy of about 20 centimetres. The OPERA anomaly was traced to an error in the geodetic survey of the baseline distance, a diagnosis that cannot be squared with a separation pinned down to roughly a fifth of a metre, for a distance known that precisely cannot be mistaken by the tens of metres a 60-nanosecond head start would require. By contrast, OPERA disclosed two faults in its timing equipment in February 2012, a disclosure that placed the suspect element in the apparatus rather than in the surveyed geometry.

Andrew Cohen and Sheldon Glashow argued that superluminal neutrinos would lose energy by emitting electron-positron pairs in flight. The ICARUS experiment observed no sign of the in-flight energy loss predicted by Cohen and Glashow. The weight of the case, in the end, lay with repetition of the measurement itself. The February disclosures came first, and the decisive remeasurements followed in the weeks after. ICARUS reported in March 2012 a neutrino time-of-flight consistent with light propagation, and that result confirms that the OPERA, ICARUS, LVD and Borexino experiments all reported neutrino velocities compatible with the speed of light. In other words, the neutrinos crossed the baseline in the same time that light would have taken, and the anomaly belonged to the instrument rather than to nature.

data.question: How did oceanographers establish whether the abrupt slowdown of Atlantic overturning circulation recorded in the 2000s reflected a long-term weakening trend or ordinary short-term variability?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The RAPID array was deployed across 41°N in 1992.
  • Model experiments showed that a single decade of monitoring is sufficient to detect an anthropogenic overturning trend.
data.a_html:
The RAPID-MOCHA array began continuous monitoring of Atlantic overturning at 26.5°N in April 2004, while Florida Current transport has been measured with a submarine telephone cable since 1982; a transport series running continuously from 1982 cannot be squared with a start of continuous transport measurement only in April 2004, so one of the two measurement histories must be wrong. The RAPID array was deployed across 41°N in 1992, a deployment history that cannot be squared with the beginning of continuous monitoring at 26.5°N in April 2004; whatever the true chronology of the moorings, these two accounts of when and where the array entered the water cannot both be correct, and settling the question of trend versus variability depended on knowing which record was actually in hand.

Overturning transport at 26.5°N fell by roughly 30% during the winter of 2009–2010, which shows that the downturn was the largest transport anomaly in the array record at the time of its observation. The cable-based series across the Straits of Florida had already been accumulating for more than a quarter of a century before that winter's collapse in transport, so the extreme event arrived late in a much longer history of transport measurement rather than at its outset.

Smeed and colleagues reported an average decline of about 0.5 Sverdrups per year between 2004 and 2012. Ocean reanalyses placed the 2000s decline within the spread of internally generated variability simulated by climate models. Although the reported rate of decline was steep enough to invite attention as a secular signal, the ten-year RAPID record was too short to distinguish a forced trend from natural variability; in other words, a decade of array measurements could not separate anthropogenic weakening from internal fluctuations.

Model experiments showed that a single decade of monitoring is sufficient to detect an anthropogenic overturning trend. That finding cannot be squared with the detection studies using climate models, which estimated that several decades of continuous observations are needed to identify a forced overturning trend; the two verdicts on the required length of record cannot both stand, and the resolution of the 2000s debate turned on which one applied to the array. The fact that the 2000s decline sits within the simulated spread of internally generated variability is what shows the 2009–2010 downturn to have reflected short-term variability rather than a long-term weakening trend, and precisely this reasoning led a review of the RAPID observations to that determination.

Whereas the array-based appraisal assigned the 2009–2010 event to short-term variability, the indirect reconstructions that reach beyond the instrumental era point instead toward a sustained, long-run decline of the circulation. Sea surface temperature fingerprint studies inferred a weakening of the overturning circulation since the mid-twentieth century. Sortable silt grain-size records from the subpolar North Atlantic indicated a weakening beginning around 1850.

data.question: How do forensic engineers establish whether a bridge collapse originated in a design deficiency or in substandard construction, and how does a subsequent authoritative inquiry settle the disagreement between the parties?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The recovered concrete cores tested below the specified 28-day compressive strength.
  • The investigation attributed the collapse to improper compaction of concrete by the contractor.
data.a_html:
Forensic reconstruction of a structural failure begins with the physical and documentary record of the hours that precede it. The pedestrian bridge at Florida International University collapsed on March 15, 2018. The casualty record admits exactly one of two accounts, with no middle ground: either six people were killed in the collapse, or no one was killed in it. Structural cracking in the span was documented in photographs taken before the collapse. The sequence of site activity is also a matter of record: post-tensioning rods in diagonal member 11 were being retensioned at the moment of the collapse.

Finite element modeling was used to recalculate the load demands at the failed connection. Analysis of this kind is referenced to as-built geometry rather than to the design drawings alone, because the governing question is always whether a member was asked to carry more than it was capable of carrying; it is that comparison of demand against delivered capacity which assigns responsibility either to the drawings or to their execution. The design firm attributed the failure to deficient construction workmanship, and that attribution led forensic engineers to extract concrete cores from the collapsed span for compressive strength testing.

The recovered concrete cores tested below the specified 28-day compressive strength, a result that indicates the design firm was right to locate the failure in deficient construction workmanship. By contrast, the construction contractor attributed the failure to errors in the structural design. Each side, in other words, pressed the explanation that lay outside its own scope of work, and the dispute narrowed to the condition of the critical nodal region where the diagonal met the deck.

Resolving such a disagreement requires asking what, precisely, was wrong with that node. At least one of two things was the case, and perhaps both: the design of the critical nodal region was deficient, or the nodal region as built departed from the project specifications. The first possibility would place the fault in the calculations that sized the connection; the second would place it in the hands that formed and cast it.

The investigation attributed the collapse to improper compaction of concrete by the contractor, a conclusion that the sub-strength cores drawn from the span confirm. That attribution, however, cannot be squared with the finding of the authoritative body: the National Transportation Safety Board determined that the probable cause of the collapse was load and capacity calculation errors made by the bridge design firm, and if those calculation errors were the probable cause, the compaction explanation is ruled out. The Board's determination is, in turn, what settles the first branch of the alternative set out above, showing the design of the critical nodal region to have been deficient.
